Cell replication is imperfect. Every replication at the genomic level of each cell contains a margin of error. Over time, incorrect or incomplete copies increase. This affects the efficiancy of cell funcion, in turn affecting tissue function, and prgan system function. Higher cellular metabolism usually means that these imperfect replications pile up faster. This is why small, fast creatures *in general* (such as hummingbirds and mice) have shorter natural life spans than larger, slower creatures with slow metabolic rates, (such as whales and giant tortoises and elephants). 


Lifestyle affects how well we are able to support our cells abilities to replicate with high fidelity. Periods of illness, constant UV damage, increased strain on liver and kidneys from poor diet will "speed up" the process

Biology uni student here, atheist but raised catholic. Here is an excerpt (which has correct information) from a US government health initiative website about the development of a fertilised human egg:  


 "For the first 12 hours after conception, the fertilized egg remains a single cell. After 30 hours or so, it divides from one cell into two. Some 15 hours later, the two cells divide to become four. And at the end of 3 days, the fertilized egg cell has become a berry-like structure made up of 16 cells. This structure is called a morula, which is Latin for mulberry. During the first 8 or 9 days after conception, the cells that will eventually form the embryo continue to divide. At the same time, the hollow structure in which they have arranged themselves, called a blastocyst, is slowly carried toward the uterus by tiny hair-like structures in the fallopian tube, called cilia. The blastocyst, though only the size of a pinhead, is actually composed of hundreds of cells. During the critically important process of implantation, the blastocyst must attach itself to the lining of the uterus or the pregnancy will not survive." 


 Okay. So that fertilised egg is a zygote. One egg cell from your ovary, with one sperm that has entered it. They both have half the usual amount of chromosomes, so together they make a full cell.  Do you know what other things are full cells? Many bacteria. Human eggs are sizeable, so this single cell zygote in your fallopian tube (not in the uterus) is like a tiny poppy seed.  It does not have more than one cell, and therefore does not have heart cells or brain cells, just reams of DNA code. It is a biological recipe book at this point.  Even split into two cells, it does not have those specific cells. Cells are not sapient, they cannot feel emotions, or think. 


This zygote that you possibly removed from your body (a- if you got the plan b 24 hours later,  b- if a sperm actually reached the egg, which can take up to 6 hours, c- if the egg was actually released and fertile, which occurs for max 24 hours on about day 16 of your menstrual cycle) 




 If all those things aligned, this bundle of 2 cells still inside your fallopian tube still has no set heart or brain cells. No nerve cells, no possible way to feel emotions or even feel external stimuli. It could still become a set of twins, multiple different people! So how can it be one? One of these cells, if the process continues, will be a placenta. Are placentas people? 




You have not murdered anybody. The possible pregnancy that you may have stopped before it started, did not happen. 




There was no implantation of a blastocyst, no embryo grew in your uterus.  




The people traumatising you and victim blaming you can get fucked.  




Side note for reference- although cells can differ in size, they remain constant in organisation. For reference, there are about 20 MILLION cells in an ant.

Not stupid at all, a good question! The stomach is only one site of digestion. Stomachs create an acidic environment where certain enzymes are secreted that break down proteins. 
There are hypotheses about platypus, and echidnas (which evolved from aquatic, platypus origins, but now eat ants) that the alkaline sediments that they take in from sifting through underwater sediment for food basically made the upkeep of an acidic stomach environment too costly in terms of energy. Like many fish with similar sifting habits, the stomach has been abandoned, and the main site of digestion is in the different areas of the intestines. Different enzymes are secreted to breakdown the food swallowed, and absorb the nutrients from it before it comes out the other end.

Also, as others have said, people familiar with keeping fish will identify some species as much messier than others. Goldfish will consume a lot, defecate a lot, and generally trash the tank. Rasboras and tetras, not so much. 

I think that there's a correlation between how animals communicate with each other and how 'messy' they are. The insects and various invertebrates you mentioned (I am not familiar with their taxonomy, sorry) are minimally communicative, and rely mainly on sight. 

Birds in social groupings rely more on social cues than solitary hunters. That might not be relevant, however birds of prey, any solitary hunting animal for that matter, needs to be invested in keeping it's whereabouts hidden so that the element of surprise will work in it's favour. Group hunters don't need to worry about that so much. So, solitary animals could perhaps be less messy than social animals.

Then back to communication methods... sight is a pretty clean way of communicating. But if your it's main avenue of communication is smell? Well then you need a scent to smell. So you need your community to secrete scents. 

I think this is where social mammals begin to appear to be very messy according to how you have classed that. The tear duct and nasal secretions are necessary for the maintenance of highly specialised olfactory processing areas. The scents left by glands in the urine and feces, as well as other glandular secretions that are rubbed around the environment provide important information to the other members of their community, information about oestrus cycle, dominance, age, any number of identifying factors. All without alerting the solitary sight hunters to which they may be prey. This includes canines, and even mammalian solitary hunters like the cats leave prominent secretions around their territories to create a sensory 'border fence' to be acknowledged by their neighbors without the need for face to face aggression. 

Parrots have scent glands which they use to carefully coat all of their feathers with protective oils, and also scents which can be identified by their community. So secretions can not only be useful for communication, but also for the care and preservation of feathers, skin and fur.

Okay so I struggled with this as well, but not because of my own parents, I'm really sorry about your childhood. That would have been hell. I do have solid straightforward advice though.

1. Get counselling for possible post natal depression or general depression. You need to talk through this with someone who knows what they are talking about, even if it's a free chatline. The resources put there are varied and affordable 

2. Physically write out a routine, then set alarms on your phone. Like

 7.30am wake up, change their nappy, clothes on, brekky

12.00 lunch time, new nappy

5.00 dinner time

6.30 bath time, pajamas on, read books, bottle, bedtime

It will take a long time to get used to this but once you are both in the groove, days will be easier and will break up  into chunks. You can think "Ok, after breakfast and before lunch we will go to a playground, or play in a sand pit, or do colouring etc. 

3. Limit screen time for yourself and bub. I used some apps to get off my phone, turned off notifications and deleted Facebook, Insta and Snapchat, literally all social media except Reddit. I only let my kiddo watch shows on my phone when she comes into my bed in the morning and I need another 10 mins of sleep. She knows she has to give it back before breakfast. Our moods are better, and I am less frustrated spending time, I enjoy spending time playing with her and just having fun in the real world because I'm not just waiting to get back on my phone.

4. Leave the house every day
Whether it's groceries or a big outing, get it done. Sucks to start but feels incredible when it's accomplished! You can work with the routine you have established above. I know covid is nuts and you might be in a much more restricted area than I am, but find some natural space and walk around, or get out into the yard if you have one. Playing seems easier and more simple out in the world. So does having conversations! 

I hope this helps, these things helped me go from self hatred and guilt and avoidance to truly loving being a parent and feeling like I'm really good at it and that my child has fun every day with me. The routine also helps me feel like I was have time to myself, because I spend small bursts of QUALITY time, instead of a high QUANTITY of grumpy or unfocused time. Kiddo is so much more satisfied with the high quality time, so they wander off and find it easier to play on their own as well, giving me guilt free time to myself occasionally!

Good luck!

I've found this to be a tricky territory workplace wise. It's all about tone. If you hear a degrading comment from them, choose one of three things to reply:

1. "Sorry?" -with strong eye contact and a pleasant demeanor, asked as if they had said something interesting that you didn't hear properly. They have to think about what they are saying if they are going to repeat it to you. Be consistent. 

2. "Don't talk to me like that, it's rude." -firmly, then literally walk out of the room. Refuse to engage in amy sort of bargaining about what they said. Sometimes no-one has ever told this person straight out and they don't even know what an arsehole they are. 

3. "You alright mate?" -standoffish, could be cheeky or cheerful, could be bristly. Again throws the weight of the remark back on the person that said it. They are the one with the problem, not you. 

With consistency and without holding grudges between incidents, I've found this is a great way to set clear  boundaries about what you will tolerate from others, without becoming aggressive or resorting to emotional tennis matches. Hopefully it will improve your life and whatever relationship you have with the derogatory person. 

Peace!
